subject: Careers
title: Workplace expectations and behaviours
lesson_success_checks: Identify the five expectations. Choose an appropriate response in a scenario. Use a short simulation to self-assess all five and select one next step with evidence. These are teaching success checks derived from the weekly outcome.
source_assessment_summary: Formative reviews; work-experience evidence may feed a later assessment. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.
accreditation: The qualification and accredited units, with any mapping confirmed by staff from actual evidence. No named scheme or awarding body.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 1, 4–8 January 2027. Friday 8 January 2027, P1. One 40-minute lesson for a pair of learners. Formative; six-week term, 4 January–12 February. Week 6 assessing. No clock time supplied.
timing: Settle, check task readiness and choose a response mode.
Introduce invented business, five expectations and one worked response.
Match scenarios, rehearse roles, check meaning and private hinge.
Tier task, two brief simulation rounds with role swap, own self-assessment.
Private evidence check, one next step and response; save individual record.

source_timing.note: The forty-minute phases are authored for this brief, not supplied by row 88.

source_adaptation: C88 exact weekly outcome retained. A88 strand shortened to Employability & Careers; D88–F88 identifying framework, resource and evidence labels expressed generically. The row supplies no minute sequence or prescribed five-item list: the 5/8/10/12/5 sequence, invented business, expectations, simulation and self-assessment implement the owner brief. No live digital tasks or personal work records. Tier labels Supported/Standard/Stretch follow this specific brief.

sources.note: Uploaded workbook snapshot read directly. B88 and C88 exact. Identifying labels A88/D88–F88 generic. Raw workbook not distributed; no current repository check claimed.
Accepted LAUNCH editions, core members, staff answers and planner style. New Public/Shared_Resources layout follows Spring instruction. Added separate tier packs and cover plans for this brief.
Unchanged generic generated work illustration bank. No external source image.

Friday 8 January P1; pair; forty minutes; theme Resilience & Change. Invented continuing small business, tiered Supported/Standard/Stretch packs, staff answers, cover plan and five-expectation self-assessment. W2–W6 one per return. Pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Match A and B using two labelled choices, a word bank and a model. Keep a short order checklist and sentence stems during simulation. Use voice, pointing, aid, typing or exact scribe. Give one evidence example and rate all five honestly.
routes.Standard: Match four cases to expectations and explain two responses. Agree roles, carry out and check the order, then complete the five-row self-assessment with an evidence example and a next step. Keep normal access aids.
routes.Stretch: Compare competing pressures in D/E and justify a response that protects quality and access. Suggest a practical adjustment, try the same order and evaluate how it helped. Use the same five-row self-assessment; more writing is optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

expectations.label: Readiness and reliability
expectations.meaning: Know the agreed start and task. Get agreed materials ready. Tell the supervisor if a delay or support need affects the plan.
expectations.look_for: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.

expectations.label: Respectful communication
expectations.meaning: Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
expectations.look_for: I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.

expectations.label: Instructions and quality
expectations.meaning: Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
expectations.look_for: I checked a step or the finished packs against the order.

expectations.label: Safety and help
expectations.meaning: Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
expectations.look_for: I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.

expectations.label: Teamwork and responsibility
expectations.meaning: Agree roles, share information and report mistakes honestly. Ask for a workable adjustment when needed.
expectations.look_for: I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

rating_states: I did this with a prompt

cases.title: An unclear step
cases.text: A worker sees an instruction they do not understand. They are about to guess so the task is finished quickly.
cases.response: Pause and ask the supervisor to explain the step. Read it back before continuing.
cases.reason: A checked instruction reduces avoidable mistakes.

cases.title: Different ideas
cases.text: The two workers both want to prepare the packs. Neither has agreed to check them.
cases.response: Agree who prepares and who checks, then swap on the next round.
cases.reason: Clear roles give both workers a way to contribute.

cases.title: A blocked route
cases.text: A worker notices an empty box in a walkway in the made-up workplace.
cases.response: Stop using that route and tell the supervisor. Follow the agreed way to make it safe.
cases.reason: Reporting a hazard protects access and safety. Do not create a real obstacle for this task.

cases.title: One item missing
cases.text: A worker is ready to report that the order is complete. The checker notices one pack has no paper strip.
cases.response: Say what is missing, add the strip using the order and check both packs again.
cases.reason: Honest checking helps improve quality; a mistake can be corrected.

cases.title: A changed start
cases.text: A worker needs help to read the task before starting. The agreed start is approaching.
cases.response: Tell the supervisor what help is needed and agree a supported start.
cases.reason: Readiness includes communicating a support need, not hiding it.

cases.title: A rushed reply
cases.text: A worker does not understand their partner’s check and replies sharply.
cases.response: Pause and ask respectfully which part needs checking. A written or aided reply is valid.
cases.reason: Respectful clarification helps people understand each other.

worked_examples_status: All worked examples, workers, business, customer roles and scenario events are invented and declared. No named employer, scheme, awarding body, provider or place. No real orders, contacts, data, payments, calls or applications.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Pass, pause and supported return are available. No personal work history, grades or family information requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet page 2 blank typed record for every tier. Book, voice, aid or exact scribe also valid. Save with lesson code/work reference and share privately. Scribe reads back and permits correction; record normal access separately from supplied thinking.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: short checklist, one instruction at a time, model and reduced cases. Communication and Interaction: processing time, rehearsal, written/aided alternatives and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable turns, private feedback, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: accessible layout, seated roles and usual aids. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 give scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only, then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: After A, ask privately whether the model checked meaning or guessed. Key: checked meaning. Ask for the action clue. For B, elicit the learner’s own role agreement. Fade answer cues only; retain model, written order and usual aids.

main_hinge.claim: Pause and ask for an explanation of an unclear instruction.

parallel_hinge.claim: Report a missing item, correct and recheck.

assessment: Keep one short individual self-assessment against the five expectations, one observed example or work reference, one next step and reply. Each expectation has a rating; Not seen today is valid. Evidence Sheet page 2 is a blank typed alternative, page 3 a staff observation record. Use books or usual aids by default.
judgement: Judge recognition, response and evidence-based reflection, not personality, eye contact, speed, confidence, accent or a real employment record. A communication aid or normal reading support does not automatically mean a prompt was needed. Record adult-supplied thinking separately. A discrepancy between self-rating and observation starts a private question, not a public challenge. Missing evidence stays visible.

evidence.description: Individual short self-assessment against five expectations, with actual example, access/prompts, one next step and response.

where_this_leads: This helps me recognise workplace expectations, ask for support and use evidence to improve a work habit.
colour_blind_safe: Expectation numbers and words, ratings and captions carry meaning without colour.

asset.description: Unchanged generic generated work symbols. Native picture crops and editable captions.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Friday 8 January 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · LAUNCH · a pair of learners · Spring 1 Week 1 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks. Week 6 is assessing. Thread tags: SMSC So/M (S/C: none); British Values MR/IL (D/RL/T: none).
Source: LAUNCH Weekly - Spring, row 88, C88. B88 Spr1·W1. Source framework and resource names are expressed generically; no registration or award completion is inferred.

Identify the five expectations. Choose an appropriate response in a scenario. Use a short simulation to self-assess all five and select one next step with evidence. These are teaching success checks derived from the weekly outcome.

An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.

Keep the same business, job roles, order and five expectations through the half-term. W2 health and safety; W3 work simulation or school-arranged placement; W4 instructions/teamwork; W5 customer service; W6 reflection. Only Week 1 is authored here.

Two sets of tiered reference packs, order card, five-expectation card, books or offline typed record and normal aids. Two large ready-cut cards and two strips per pair, plus spares. Use safe, accessible surfaces. No live workplace contact or personal records. Confirm the trusted adult and pause/return route.
This helps me recognise workplace expectations, ask for support and use evidence to improve a work habit.
Settle, check task readiness and choose a response mode.
Introduce invented business, five expectations and one worked response.
Match scenarios, rehearse roles, check meaning and private hinge.
Tier task, two brief simulation rounds with role swap, own self-assessment.
Private evidence check, one next step and response; save individual record.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes. These phases are a teaching design; row 88 gives no minute sequence. Processing and brief pauses included. Slides 7 and 8 share 23–35 minutes.

0–5: welcome privately, show the order and ask what would help someone start it. Offer a neutral example and a pass. 5–9: introduce business, roles and five expectations. 9–13: model A: pause, ask what a step means, read it back. Model a self-check with an actual observed example, not a prefilled learner answer.

13–19: match A/B to instructions/teamwork, then use additional cases as appropriate. Rehearse preparer/checker roles with the order in view. Respectful communication includes aids and asking for time. 19–23: hinge: unclear task, A guess and rush or B pause and ask. Key B. Parallel: missing strip, A report and correct then check or B hide it; key A. Re-model and recheck privately.

23–26: use the chosen Supported/Standard/Stretch prompt; do not require every case. 26–31: two short rounds of the paper order, resetting and swapping roles, with an adult taking the partner role if needed. Each learner should have a chance to ask/check and give an update. 31–35: self-assess the five expectations using actual task evidence. Mark unobserved expectations Not seen today. Reduce scenario repetitions to protect access and reflection time.

35–38: privately compare one self-rating with a task clue, keep the first response, give one NS and retain the reply. 38–40: learner names one achievable next step and help, then save their individual self-assessment. E actual banked evidence; R only after Voice, Audience, NS and reply. No public score comparison.

Match A and B using two labelled choices, a word bank and a model. Keep a short order checklist and sentence stems during simulation. Use voice, pointing, aid, typing or exact scribe. Give one evidence example and rate all five honestly.

Match four cases to expectations and explain two responses. Agree roles, carry out and check the order, then complete the five-row self-assessment with an evidence example and a next step. Keep normal access aids.

Compare competing pressures in D/E and justify a response that protects quality and access. Suggest a practical adjustment, try the same order and evaluate how it helped. Use the same five-row self-assessment; more writing is optional.
Route names follow this specific brief. Each has its own DOCX/PDF pack and the same five expectations and evidence goal. Learners can change route with staff; a route is not a label of ability.

After A, ask privately whether the model checked meaning or guessed. Key: checked meaning. Ask for the action clue. For B, elicit the learner’s own role agreement. Fade answer cues only; retain model, written order and usual aids.

Cognition and Learning: short checklist, one instruction at a time, model and reduced cases. Communication and Interaction: processing time, rehearsal, written/aided alternatives and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable turns, private feedback, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: accessible layout, seated roles and usual aids. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 give scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only, then return task.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Pass, pause and supported return are available. No personal work history, grades or family information requested.

Keep one short individual self-assessment against the five expectations, one observed example or work reference, one next step and reply. Each expectation has a rating; Not seen today is valid. Evidence Sheet page 2 is a blank typed alternative, page 3 a staff observation record. Use books or usual aids by default.

Judge recognition, response and evidence-based reflection, not personality, eye contact, speed, confidence, accent or a real employment record. A communication aid or normal reading support does not automatically mean a prompt was needed. Record adult-supplied thinking separately. A discrepancy between self-rating and observation starts a private question, not a public challenge. Missing evidence stays visible.

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual evidence banked. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and learner reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Give one specific NS such as checking both packs or making a clarification request. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any accredited mapping.

A workplace expectation does not mean obeying an unsafe or unclear request. Pause, check and seek help. Respect does not require eye contact or public speech. Reliability includes communicating a support need. A mistake can prompt a correction. This classroom record does not prove placement attendance, employment readiness, legal compliance or a qualification.

Use the separate one-page Cover Plan for immediate delivery. Keep business and expectation wording for Weeks 2–6, one per return. No later week is authored. Further GROW Careers remains paused. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures; keep concerns outside shared evidence.

Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.

Private review, NS/reply and save evidence.

If rating and observation differ, ask privately for the clue and record any revision. A pass is unobserved. E work actually saved; R only after Voice, Audience, NS and reply. Offer to Communication portfolio.
Task guides only. These are not observations of learners.
Primary expectation: Instructions and quality. Pause and ask the supervisor to explain the step. Read it back before continuing. A checked instruction reduces avoidable mistakes.
Primary expectation: Teamwork and responsibility. Agree who prepares and who checks, then swap on the next round. Clear roles give both workers a way to contribute.

Primary expectation: Safety and help. Stop using that route and tell the supervisor. Follow the agreed way to make it safe. Reporting a hazard protects access and safety. Do not create a real obstacle for this task.

Accept another expectation where the learner explains it from the facts. A clarification request can show respectful communication as well as instruction checking. Do not require a single memorised label.
Primary expectation: Instructions and quality. Say what is missing, add the strip using the order and check both packs again. Honest checking helps improve quality; a mistake can be corrected.
Primary expectation: Readiness and reliability. Tell the supervisor what help is needed and agree a supported start. Readiness includes communicating a support need, not hiding it.
Primary expectation: Respectful communication. Pause and ask respectfully which part needs checking. A written or aided reply is valid. Respectful clarification helps people understand each other.

Correct finished order: two packs, each with one large card and one paper strip; both checked against the order and ready status communicated. Learners may keep the order in view. Reset and swap roles. Adult can partner for private access. Do not judge speed or manufacture a real hazard.
Model: checked meaning. Main hinge B: pause and ask. Parallel A: report missing strip, correct and recheck. Re-model one step if unclear; recheck privately. Pass is unobserved.

Keep all five self-ratings, at least one actual example and one next step with help/time. A missing opportunity is Not seen today. There is no required “best” rating and no personality score. Normal communication/reading aids are access, not automatically an answer prompt. Record supplied thinking separately. Compare a rating with an actual clue privately; retain any changed judgement.

Supported: choices, word bank, frames and checklist. Standard: four cases and two explained responses. Stretch: competing pressures, a justified response and adjustment. Each completes the same order and self-assessment. Route names Supported/Standard/Stretch follow this brief. No forced public speaking or personal account.

One NS and reply; R after Voice, Audience, NS and response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. E only actual saved work. Private help through trusted adult or school route; pass, pause and return. Listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.

Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
